    WELCOME TO THE DAILY MARKET

    Small robot. Thoughtful decisions.

    Retail Run is a classroom simulation of a smart retail store. Choose a mission, department, quantity and search algorithm, then dispatch Pip. The route is planned over a four-direction weighted grid.

    Run an autonomous shift

    Turn on Autopilot once. Pip prioritizes charging below 35%, restocking shelves at 4 units or less, then incoming customer orders. New orders arrive every 12 simulation seconds. Turn on Live environment for temporary trolley, spill and crate blockages every 14 seconds; they clear after 18 seconds. Drop a blockage targets the planned route when possible. Coral shows the old route; green shows the new one. Pause freezes tasks and events. Turning autopilot off lets the active mission finish.

    Make the floor come alive

    Place an obstacle on an empty aisle to trigger replanning. Click it again to remove it. Rush hour makes the central aisle more expensive. Pip stops if no route exists and retries when the floor changes. Pause freezes simulation time; reset restores the same store.

    Follow the mission

    Picking visits a shelf and then the pickup desk. Restocking visits the stockroom first. Customer guidance meets a shopper at the entrance before visiting the shelf. Inspection visits every department checkpoint. Battery consumption follows travel cost; leave enough energy to return to the charger.

    Understand the AI

    A* uses Manhattan distance with a minimum move cost of one. UCS minimizes weighted cost without a heuristic. BFS minimizes moves; DFS follows traversal order; Greedy chooses the closest estimated goal. A* and UCS are optimal for the current map snapshot, not an unknown future. The workbench separately demonstrates CSP allocation and Minimax with Alpha-Beta pruning.

    Scope and assumptions

    The store is fully observable and discrete. Shopper artwork is decorative; rush-hour costs and user-placed obstacles are the dynamic inputs. Scheduling and service planning are interactive teaching models, not simultaneous multi-robot motion. No real sensors, payments, or machine-learning model are connected.
